most_likely: Refractory ventricular tachycardia in non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy with LVAD
summary: Middle-aged/older man with non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy (EF <20%) s/p HeartMate II LVAD, listed status 1A(b) for heart transplant, admitted after a single ICD shock while on a fishing trip. Device interrogation showed one shock plus >20 VT episodes aborted by ATP despite maximal antiarrhythmic therapy (quinidine, mexiletine, metoprolol); he underwent a repeat left stellate ganglion block with no further VT on telemetry. He also had a week of increased lower extremity edema with JVD 14 cm on admission, managed by diuretic adjustment (torsemide held then resumed), discharged near-euvolemic at 120.4 kg.

opposing_evidence: No VT recorded on telemetry after block
differential.reasoning: The entire admission was driven by documented recurrent VT despite maximal antiarrhythmic therapy, requiring an invasive sympathetic block; this is the billable principal disease rather than the shock event.
differential.coding_reason: Admitted after appropriate ICD shock; interrogation showed >20 VT events treated with ATP; stellate ganglion block performed.
